From a Roosevelt Ave cart to a Queens institution

Before there was a restaurant, there was a cart. Maria Piedad Cano — a former lawyer and judge who came to New York from Colombia in the 1980s — set up on Roosevelt Avenue near 79th Street and griddled arepas late into the night. Word traveled the way it only does in Queens: the sweet-corn arepa de choclo, crisp at the edges and molten with cheese, became a pilgrimage.

The cart grew into this dining room on 37th Avenue — the original restaurant, now carried on by her sons — with the same menu the sidewalk fell for: choclo and queso arepas, rellenas stuffed to order, patacones, and the house sauces people ask about by name.

“Originally known for slinging cheesy, golden arepas from her famed street cart on Roosevelt Avenue.” — Fodor's Travel
